newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers to review Finnish and Dutch deficits.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to review Finnish and Dutch deficits.

text.p: Finland and the Netherlands are expected to be taken off the list of European Union countries with so-called excessive deficits when EU finance ministers meet on Monday.

Having made considerable progress in improving their fiscal situation in 1996, the two countries are seen joining a small core of EU governments which are in compliance with the Maastricht treaty's target requirements for a single currency.

The addition of the Netherlands and Finland will mean that five EU governments have their budget deficits and debt levels in line with Maastricht. The other three which are already in compliance are Luxembourg, Ireland and Denmark.
Governments seeking to join a single currency should bring their 1997 budget deficits down to three percent of gross domestic product and demonstrate sustainable budgetary consolidation.
In addition, outstanding debt must approach 60 percent of GDP at a satisfactory pace.
